podcast.title: Voice Polish Comparison (1975)
podcast.body: Critic Robert Hull, when evaluating Olivia Newton-John's vocal quality, cited Leslie Gore as possessing a more "polish" to her voice. "True, her voice ain't got the polish of Karen Carpenter, Leslie Gore or Brenda Lee."

podcast.title: Feminist and LGBTQ Icon
podcast.body: Decades after her hits, Leslie Gore not only became a feminist icon due to songs like "You Don't Own Me," but also an LGBTQ advocate after she publicly came out. She spoke highly of her producer, Quincy Jones, in an interview with Rolling Stone. "Decades later, Gore, who not only became a feminist icon but an LGBTQ advocate after she came out, told Rolling Stone, quote, Quincy was a great mentor and a wonderful teacher. You can't match a genius like Quincy Jones, unquote."

podcast.title: Quincy Jones's Discovery
podcast.body: Quincy Jones personally signed Leslie Gore (birth name Leslie Sue Goldstein), a white Jewish teenager from Tenafly, New Jersey, to Mercury Records. Jones noted her "mellow distinctive voice" and her ability to "sing in tune," a quality he found lacking in many adult rock and roll singers of the time. "Of this discovery, a white Jewish teenager from Tenefly, New Jersey, Jones later wrote, quote, she had a mellow distinctive voice and sang in tune, which a lot of grown-up rock and roll singers couldn't do. So I signed her, unquote."
